title: Redux vs MobX
definition: A comparison between Redux's strict, immutable, functional architecture and MobX's mutable, observable-based reactive architecture.
simpleExplanation: Redux is strict math: state is completely frozen, and you dispatch actions to generate new copies. MobX is magic: state is fully mutable. You literally just write `state.user.name = 'John'`, and MobX automatically 'observes' the change and magically updates any React component looking at that data.
realWorldExample: A team of object-oriented Java developers often prefers MobX because it relies heavily on Classes and mutability. A team of functional programming enthusiasts prefers Redux.

basic: Which library relies on strict Immutable Updates: Redux or MobX?
intermediate: Why is debugging sometimes considered harder in MobX than in Redux?

answers.question: Which relies on Immutable?
answers.answer: Redux. (MobX explicitly relies on Mutable data).

answers.question: Why debugging harder?
answers.answer: Because MobX data can be mutated from ANYWHERE at ANY TIME. There is no strict 'Action -> Dispatch -> Reducer' trail. Redux DevTools provides a flawless, time-stamped history of exactly WHY the state changed, which is invaluable.
